tool.name: Windowed LD Calculator
tool.description: Computes LD (r²) for SNPs within a genomic window

param.name: genotypes_file
param.label: QC'd Genotypes File
param.help: Genotype data that has passed QC.

param.name: snp_annot_file
param.label: SNP Annotation File
param.help: File with SNP info (chrom, pos, maf). The output from Tool 2 is ideal.

param.name: focal_snp
param.label: Focal SNP ID
param.help: The ID of the SNP to center the window on (e.g., a top hit from your GWAS).

param.name: window_kb
param.label: Window Size (in kb)
param.help: The size of the window on each side of the focal SNP.

param.name: min_maf
param.label: Minimum MAF Threshold
param.help: SNPs with MAF below this value will be excluded.

param.name: missing_val
param.label: Missing Value Representation
param.help: The string used to denote missing genotypes.

tool.help:
**What it does**
This tool calculates Linkage Disequilibrium (LD) for a set of SNPs within a specified genomic region. LD is the non-random association of alleles at different loci. It is typically measured by r-squared (r²).
This is useful for fine-mapping a GWAS signal. After identifying a significant SNP, you can use this tool to see which other nearby SNPs are correlated with it, helping to identify the functional region.
**Inputs**
- **QC'd Genotypes File:** The filtered genotype data. - **SNP Annotation File:** A file containing chromosome, position, and MAF for each SNP. The output from the Allele Frequency Calculator is perfect for this. - **Focal SNP ID:** You must provide the ID of a SNP to act as the center of your window. This is typically the most significant SNP from your association test.
**Outputs**
- **LD Matrix (tabular):** A table containing the pairwise r² values for all SNPs in the window. - **LD Heatmap (PNG):** A graphical representation of the LD matrix, where darker colors indicate stronger correlation (higher r²).
